intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day longtail boat tour around the stunning Phi Phi archipelago, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, exploring Viking Cave, and swimming at Monkey Beach. One of Thailand's most iconic island-hopping experiences with breathtaking limestone karst scenery.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Crawl
experiences.description: Dive deep into Bangkok's legendary street food scene at Yaowarat Road (Chinatown), sampling pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, boat noodles, and fresh seafood. Join a guided food walk or explore independently through the bustling night market stalls and open-air restaurants.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Beach Hopping by Scooter
experiences.description: Rent a scooter and spend the day discovering Koh Lanta's diverse beaches — from the lively Long Beach to the secluded Bamboo Bay and the dramatic Kantiang Bay. Stop at local beachside shacks for fresh coconuts and grilled fish, experiencing a more laid-back and authentic Thai island atmosphere.

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Old City Temple & Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the ancient walled city of Chiang Mai, visiting Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phra Singh before diving into the famous Saturday or Sunday Walking Street market. Taste northern Thai specialties like khao soi (curry noodle soup), sai oua (herb sausage), and nam prik noom (green chili dip) from local vendors.

experiences.name: Similan Islands Liveaboard Snorkel & Dive Trip
experiences.description: Join an overnight or day-trip liveaboard to the world-renowned Similan Islands National Park, considered one of Asia's top dive and snorkel destinations. Encounter vibrant coral reefs, sea turtles, reef sharks, and manta rays in some of the clearest waters in the Andaman Sea.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage. Take an affordable airport bus or shared minivan to your hotel area to save on transfer costs. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: Meal on flight or skip
meals.lunch: Meal on flight or airport food court
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack from a 7-Eleven or nearby night street food stall near the hotel (pad kra pao or grilled skewers for under 60 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 22:30 arrival. Exchange some currency at the airport for better rates than hotel exchange. Grab a local SIM card at the airport (approx 299 THB for 30 days data) for cheap navigation and communication throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a slow start, walk down to the beachfront and enjoy your first glimpse of the Thai coastline. Take a leisurely stroll along the beach near Aegean Bliss Resort, watch local fishermen, and breathe in the sea air. Explore the immediate hotel surroundings and get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local market or walking street for an orientation stroll. Visit a nearby Buddhist temple (wat) for free cultural immersion — most temples are open to visitors at no charge. Rent a bicycle or scooter (150–250 THB/day) to explore the local beach road and nearby villages at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Find the local night market or beach road street food strip. Sample classic Thai street food including pad thai, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut. Watch the sunset from the beach before heading back to rest and plan the upcoming days.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or local coffee shop with khao tom (rice porridge) for 50–80 THB
meals.lunch: Street food stall near the beach — som tam (papaya salad) and sticky rice for under 80 THB
meals.dinner: Night market street food — pad thai, grilled corn, fresh fruit smoothies. Budget 150–200 THB total

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today to adjust to the time zone. October is shoulder/low season in Thailand which means fewer crowds and lower prices — great for budget travelers. Check weather forecasts as October can bring occasional rain showers.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise beach walk. Head to the local pier or ferry terminal and book a budget day-trip boat tour to nearby islands. Many local operators offer shared longtail boat tours for 300–500 THB per person. Depart by 9:00 AM to maximize island time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Island hopping adventure — visit 2 to 3 nearby smaller islands. Snorkel in clear turquoise waters (bring your own snorkel gear or rent for 100 THB), explore hidden coves, and relax on white sand beaches. Pack snacks and water from a convenience store to save money on island vendor prices.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon. Shower and freshen up at the hotel. Head out to a local seafood restaurant or beachside barbecue shack for fresh grilled fish — look for places with plastic chairs and Thai-language menus for the best prices (200–300 THB for a full seafood meal).

meals.breakfast: Early morning — grab a fresh baguette with egg or roti with banana from a street cart for 40–60 THB
meals.lunch: Pack a convenience store lunch (7-Eleven onigiri, sandwiches, instant noodles) to eat on the island boat trip — budget 80–120 THB
meals.dinner: Local seafood BBQ shack near the pier — grilled fish, morning glory stir fry, jasmine rice. Budget 200–300 THB

day_by_day.notes: Book island tours directly with local longtail boat operators at the pier rather than through hotel concierge or travel agencies to save 30–50% on tour costs. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local fresh market (talat sod) early in the morning around 7:00–9:00 AM for an authentic Thai experience. Watch vendors sell tropical fruits, fresh fish, vegetables, and local snacks. Try fresh-cut fruit (40 THB), fried dough sticks (patongo) with pandan custard, and Thai iced coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (200–250 THB/day) and explore the coastal road independently. Stop at viewpoints, hidden beaches, and local fishing villages. Visit a free public beach away from tourist crowds. Look for a small family-run restaurant for a simple Thai lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area and explore the local walking street or night bazaar. Browse handmade crafts, clothing, and souvenirs — practice bargaining politely for better prices. Enjoy street food snacks while walking.

meals.breakfast: Fresh market breakfast — tropical fruit, fried dough sticks, Thai iced coffee. Budget 60–100 THB
meals.lunch: Local family restaurant (raan khao) — order a rice plate with stir-fried basil and egg (khao pad kra pao kai) for 60–80 THB
meals.dinner: Night bazaar street food crawl — try 4 to 5 different small dishes: satay skewers, spring rolls, mango sticky rice, coconut ice cream. Budget 150–200 THB

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental is the most cost-effective and flexible way to explore the area. Always wear a helmet and carry your passport or a copy. Check if your travel insurance covers scooter riding.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer ferry or speedboat journey to a more distant island destination (book tickets the night before at a pier travel desk for best prices). Popular budget options include Ko Lanta, Ko Phi Phi, Ko Tao, or Ko Chang depending on your base location. Depart early to maximize time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the new island on foot or by renting a bicycle. Visit the main beach, snorkel off the shore, and discover local beach bars and budget bungalows. Swim in calm bays and look for sea turtles or colorful fish in shallow reef areas.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from a beachside spot with a cold Chang or Singha beer (60–80 THB) or a fresh coconut. Enjoy a beachside dinner at a budget beach restaurant — many offer set meals with soup, main course, and rice for 150–250 THB.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel or pier-side coffee shop before ferry departure — toast with eggs and Thai tea for 80 THB
meals.lunch: Beach shack on the island — green curry with rice or fried rice with vegetables for 100–150 THB
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant on the island — tom yum soup, fish with garlic and pepper, steamed rice. Budget 200–250 THB

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets for island hopping typically cost 150–400 THB per leg depending on distance. Book round-trip tickets for slight savings. October weather may mean some ferry services are reduced — always confirm schedules the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: If staying overnight on the island, enjoy a morning snorkel directly from the beach before crowds arrive. Many islands have excellent reef access right from the shore at no cost. Alternatively, join a budget group snorkel tour (300–400 THB) to nearby snorkel spots with better coral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to a viewpoint on the island for panoramic ocean views — most island viewpoint trails are free and take 30–60 minutes. Alternatively, kayak around the island coastline (kayak rental typically 100–150 THB per hour) to discover sea caves and hidden lagoons.
day_by_day.evening: Take the return ferry back to your base. Arrive by early evening and freshen up. Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage near the hotel (250–350 THB for 1 hour) as a budget-friendly reward after days of activity.

meals.breakfast: Island guesthouse or beach café breakfast — banana pancake and fresh juice for 80–120 THB
meals.lunch: Pack convenience store snacks for the ferry ride back or eat at the pier food stall — noodle soup for 60–80 THB
meals.dinner: Back at base — find a local Thai restaurant away from tourist areas for authentic khao man gai (poached chicken rice) or boat noodles. Budget 80–120 THB

day_by_day.notes: Traditional Thai massage is one of Thailand's best budget luxuries. Avoid overpriced tourist massage shops on main streets — look for local community massage centers or temple-affiliated massage schools for authentic and affordable sessions.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning at the hotel beachfront. Take a long swim in the ocean and relax on the beach. Read a book, journal, or simply enjoy the tropical atmosphere. Visit a nearby café for a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local village or town center on foot or by tuk-tuk (negotiate fare before boarding, typically 50–100 THB for short distances). Visit a local convenience store or small supermarket to stock up on snacks and drinks for upcoming island trips. Find a shaded spot and plan the remaining days of your trip.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or low-cost beach bonfire or social gathering if available at the hotel or nearby beach bar. Meet other budget travelers and exchange tips. Enjoy a simple dinner and early night to prepare for more adventures.

meals.breakfast: Beachside café — acai bowl or fruit smoothie bowl with granola for 120–150 THB (a slight splurge on rest day)
meals.lunch: 7-Eleven or FamilyMart — pick up ready-made Thai dishes, cup noodles, or sandwiches. Budget 60–100 THB
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant — massaman curry with roti bread and a fresh lime soda. Budget 150–200 THB

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest days are important for sustainable budget travel. Use this time to do laundry at a local laundromat (self-service costs 30–60 THB per load) and reorganize your backpack.

day_by_day.morning: Book an early morning budget cooking class (look for small group classes run by local families rather than large tourist operations — costs 600–900 THB vs 1500+ THB at resorts). Learn to make 3 classic Thai dishes: pad thai, green curry, and tom kha soup. Visit a local market with the instructor to buy ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: After cooking class (usually ends by noon), head to a beach for afternoon relaxation. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP rental typically 200–300 THB per hour) or simply swim and snorkel. Look for free beach volleyball games with locals or other travelers.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a different part of the beach road or town for dinner. Look for a night market or food court style eating area where multiple vendors operate — great for sampling variety on a budget. Try dishes you haven't eaten yet: khao soi, larb, or nam tok.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before cooking class — fresh fruit and coffee from a street cart for 50–70 THB
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you cooked in the cooking class — this is typically included in the class price
meals.dinner: Night market food court — try 3 to 4 different vendor dishes for a varied meal. Budget 150–200 THB total

day_by_day.notes: Budget cooking classes are an excellent investment — you learn skills to take home and get a meal included. Search Facebook groups or hostel notice boards for small local classes. Avoid hotel-branded cooking experiences which are significantly more expensive.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning long-tail boat or kayak through mangrove forests or sea caves if available in your area (group tours start at 400–600 THB). Mangrove ecosystems are fascinating and the early morning light is beautiful for photos. Look for monitor lizards, monkeys, and exotic birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park beach or protected marine area. Many national park beaches charge a small entrance fee (200 THB for foreigners) but offer pristine, less-crowded environments. Snorkel, swim, and picnic on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel and freshen up. Head to a local beachside bar for happy hour (many bars offer 2-for-1 drinks from 5–7 PM). Watch the sunset and socialize. Have dinner at a nearby Thai restaurant specializing in southern Thai cuisine — spicier and more coconut-heavy than central Thai food.

meals.breakfast: Early morning — instant coffee and a banana or energy bar before the mangrove tour. Pack extra snacks.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the national park beach — pick up supplies from a convenience store the night before: fruits, crackers, cheese, and drinks. Budget 100–150 THB
meals.dinner: Southern Thai restaurant — gaeng tai pla (southern fish curry) or khua kling (dry curry) with rice. Budget 100–150 THB

day_by_day.notes: National park fees support conservation efforts. Always bring your own water and snacks to national parks as vendors inside charge premium prices. Respect wildlife and do not feed monkeys as it disrupts their natural behavior.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a larger nearby island or coastal town via public ferry or bus (much cheaper than tourist minivans). Explore the local town market, visit a hilltop temple with ocean views, and wander through streets lined with Sino-Portuguese architecture if visiting areas like Phuket Old Town or Krabi Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the town — visit a local museum or cultural center (entrance fees typically 50–100 THB or free). Browse local shops for authentic Thai products at local prices. Try a local dessert shop for khanom (Thai sweets) and cold drinks.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to your base in the early evening. Stop for dinner at a hawker-style food center. Spend the evening at the hotel beach, stargazing and reflecting on the trip so far.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or coffee shop in the town you're visiting — croissant or toast with local jam and coffee for 80–100 THB
meals.lunch: Hawker food center in the town — choose from multiple stalls. Noodle soup, fried rice, or grilled meat over rice. Budget 60–100 THB
meals.dinner: Back at base — simple street food dinner near the hotel. Grilled pork skewers, papaya salad, sticky rice. Budget 100–150 THB

day_by_day.notes: Use local public songthaew (shared pickup trucks) and buses instead of tourist transfers for significant savings — a local bus may cost 50 THB vs 300 THB for a tourist minivan on the same route.

day_by_day.morning: Final major island hopping day — book a full-day budget group tour to the most iconic island cluster in the area (e.g., Phi Phi Islands, Similan Islands, or Ang Thong Marine Park). Shared speedboat tours typically cost 800–1200 THB and include multiple stops, snorkeling, and lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the afternoon portion of the full-day tour — snorkeling at coral reefs, swimming in emerald lagoons, and visiting iconic viewpoints. Take plenty of photos and soak in the stunning scenery. This is the highlight island experience of the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Return from tour by late afternoon. Treat yourself to a sit-down restaurant dinner to celebrate the near-end of the trip. Splurge slightly on a nicer local restaurant (still budget-friendly at 300–400 THB for a full meal with drinks) and try a Thai dessert platter.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or quick street food before tour departure — roti with condensed milk and coffee for 60 THB
meals.lunch: Included in the full-day tour package — typically a basic Thai buffet on an island or at a beach restaurant
meals.dinner: Slightly nicer local seafood restaurant — whole grilled sea bass, morning glory, tom yum soup, rice and a cold beer. Budget 300–400 THB

day_by_day.notes: Full-day island tours are best booked 1–2 days in advance directly at pier booking offices. Compare prices between 2 to 3 operators. Confirm what is included: snorkel equipment, national park fees, lunch, and transfers. October may have weather variability so check conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning in Thailand. Wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach. Take a slow walk along the shoreline, collect shells, and reflect on the journey. Visit any local spots you missed — a temple, a viewpoint, or a café you've been meaning to try.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at the local market or night bazaar. Buy practical Thai souvenirs on a budget: Thai tea bags (80 THB), coconut oil (100 THB), handmade soap, silk scarves, or elephant pants. Practice final bargaining skills. Pack your bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.evening: Final Thai dinner — return to your favorite street food spot or restaurant from the trip. Order all your favorite dishes one last time. Take photos of the food and the surroundings. Enjoy a final sunset beach walk and say goodbye to the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Favorite local breakfast spot — perhaps the same market stall you visited on Day 3. Khao tom or jok (rice congee) with a Thai iced tea for 80 THB
meals.lunch: Street food lunch near the market — mix of dishes from different stalls. Budget 150 THB
meals.dinner: Final dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip — order generously for a celebratory last meal. Budget 250–350 THB

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure is later in the day. Most hotels offer free luggage storage. Convert remaining Thai Baht back to your home currency at the airport or keep some for future trips as airport exchange rates are less favorable.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. Wake up according to your flight schedule. Enjoy a final simple breakfast. Do a final check of the hotel room for any left-behind items — chargers, toiletries, travel documents. Take a last look at the beachfront view from Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to the airport with plenty of time to spare — allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Use a budget transfer option: public bus, shared minivan, or pre-booked Grab car. Complete airport check-in, immigration, and security. Browse duty-free for any last-minute gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, island hopping, and street food adventures across Thailand. Review your budget spending and plan your next budget adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — one last bowl of noodle soup or fried rice from a local stall near the hotel for 60–80 THB
meals.lunch: Airport food court — more affordable than airport restaurants. Look for local Thai food stalls in the terminal. Budget 150–200 THB
meals.dinner: Meal on the flight or airport restaurant before boarding

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for 13 days: Accommodation at Aegean Bliss Resort (varies), daily food budget 300–500 THB, island tours 800–1200 THB each, transport 50–400 THB per journey, activities 200–600 THB per day. Total estimated daily budget excluding accommodation: 1500–2500 THB (approximately $40–$70 USD) per day for a comfortable budget experience.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and arrange private transfer or airport taxi to your hotel. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up.

meals.breakfast: Skip or eat on the plane
meals.lunch: Skip or eat on the plane
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from a 7-Eleven or airport food court upon arrival — try a Thai-style rice bowl or instant noodles to keep it simple and affordable

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives late at night. Focus solely on reaching the hotel safely. Keep some Thai Baht handy for transport. Pre-book airport transfer if possible to avoid stress upon arrival. Rest well for the adventures ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront to get your first feel of Thailand's coastline. Explore the resort grounds and orient yourself with the surrounding area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local beach area for a relaxed afternoon. Rent a beach chair and umbrella (approx 100-150 THB), swim in the warm Gulf of Thailand waters, and soak up the tropical atmosphere. Visit a nearby viewpoint or beachside temple if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the nearest night market or beach walking street. Browse street food stalls, try local snacks, and get your first taste of authentic Thai street food culture. Watch a traditional Thai cultural performance if available nearby.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — enjoy tropical fruits, congee, and Thai-style eggs
meals.lunch: Beachside seafood shack — try grilled fish with sticky rice and som tum (green papaya salad) for around 150-200 THB
meals.dinner: Night market street food crawl — pad thai from a wok stall (60-80 THB), mango sticky rice (50 THB), and fresh coconut water (30 THB)

day_by_day.notes: October is part of Thailand's rainy season in some regions. Carry a light rain poncho. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen. Exchange currency at a reputable exchange booth rather than the airport for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a local floating market or fresh produce market to experience the vibrant local food culture. Watch vendors sell tropical fruits, fresh seafood, and Thai snacks from boats or stalls. Pick up fresh fruit for a healthy snack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat tour of the surrounding coastal area. Explore hidden lagoons, mangrove forests, and sea caves. Many tours depart from the main pier and cost 400-800 THB per person for a 2-3 hour excursion.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel, freshen up, and enjoy a sunset cocktail at a beachfront bar. Watch the sun dip below the horizon over the water. Explore a local restaurant strip for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and Thai-style breakfast from the morning market — try khao tom (rice soup) with condiments for 50-80 THB
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack from the market before the boat tour, or enjoy lunch at a pier-side restaurant with fresh seafood
meals.dinner: Mid-range Thai restaurant near the resort — order tom yum goong (spicy shrimp soup), pad kra pao (basil stir-fry), and jasmine rice for around 250-350 THB per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the longtail boat tour through your hotel concierge or a reputable local agency. Wear comfortable water-resistant shoes and bring a dry bag for valuables. October weather may bring brief afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Island hopping day trip! Board a speedboat or ferry to a nearby island group. Visit snorkeling spots with vibrant coral reefs and colorful tropical fish. Bring your own snorkel gear or rent it on-site for 100-150 THB.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping to a second island. Explore a quieter beach away from the crowds, hike to a viewpoint for panoramic ocean views, or kayak through emerald green waters. Many day trips include 3-4 island stops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the mainland by late afternoon. Rest at the hotel before heading out for a casual beachside dinner. Share travel stories with fellow travelers at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — fuel up with protein and carbs
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the tour operator, or eat at a beach restaurant on one of the islands — fresh grilled squid and fried rice (150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Casual beachfront restaurant — try massaman curry with roti bread and a cold Chang beer for around 300 THB

day_by_day.notes: Book the island hopping tour at least one day in advance. Tours typically cost 800-1500 THB per person including transport, snorkeling equipment, and sometimes lunch. Bring waterproof sunscreen, a hat, and a towel. Check weather forecasts before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Thai cooking class offered by a local chef or cooking school. Learn to make 3-4 classic dishes including pad thai, green curry, and tom kha gai. Classes typically run 3-4 hours and cost 800-1200 THB including ingredients and a recipe booklet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local temple (wat) in the area. Admire intricate Buddhist architecture, golden chedis, and ornate murals. Dress respectfully with shoulders and knees covered. Explore the temple grounds and observe monks going about their daily routines.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a vibrant night bazaar or street food market for dinner. Try dishes you haven't sampled yet and pick up handmade souvenirs, Thai silk scarves, or locally crafted jewelry.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery with fresh-baked croissants and Thai iced coffee (cafe boran)
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you prepared in the cooking class — a rewarding and delicious mid-day meal
meals.dinner: Night bazaar street food — try khao man gai (poached chicken rice), satay skewers, and roti with condensed milk for under 200 THB total

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes are a fantastic way to connect with Thai culture and bring skills home. Book in advance as popular classes fill up quickly. Temple visits are free but donations are appreciated. Remove shoes before entering any temple building.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or bicycle and explore the local countryside and coastal roads at your own pace. Discover hidden beaches, local fishing villages, and scenic viewpoints that tour buses don't reach. Scooter rentals cost approximately 200-300 THB per day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local elephant sanctuary or wildlife conservation center for an ethical wildlife encounter. Observe elephants in their natural habitat, learn about conservation efforts, and support responsible tourism. Avoid any venues that offer elephant riding.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage at a reputable spa or massage parlor. A 1-hour Thai massage costs 250-400 THB. Finish the evening with a relaxed dinner near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Street-side vendor breakfast — try khanom krok (coconut rice pancakes) and fresh-squeezed orange juice for 50-80 THB
meals.lunch: Local village restaurant discovered during your scooter ride — order whatever the locals are eating for an authentic experience (100-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual Thai restaurant — splurge slightly on a seafood platter with steamed fish in lime and chili sauce, served with rice and vegetables (400-600 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Always wear a helmet when riding a scooter and carry your international driving permit. Ethical elephant sanctuaries typically cost 1500-2500 THB for a half-day experience. Research sanctuaries carefully and choose those certified by responsible tourism organizations.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry or speedboat to a more remote island for an overnight or day trip. Explore pristine beaches with fewer tourists, crystal-clear water, and lush jungle interior. Hike a jungle trail to a waterfall or hidden viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon snorkeling at a coral reef near the island. Look for sea turtles, reef sharks, and hundreds of tropical fish species. Alternatively, try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) or kayaking around the island's coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a beachside bonfire dinner at a rustic beach bar on the island, or return to the mainland for dinner. Watch fire dancers perform traditional shows while sipping a tropical cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Resort or hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Island beach shack — fresh coconut, grilled corn, and a simple noodle soup (100-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachside barbecue restaurant — choose your fresh seafood from an ice display and have it grilled to order with garlic butter or Thai herbs (300-500 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-October may bring occasional rain showers in southern Thailand. Always check ferry schedules and weather conditions before heading to remote islands. Bring cash as ATMs may not be available on smaller islands.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning. Enjoy a slow breakfast and take a yoga or meditation class on the beach if available at the resort or a nearby wellness center. Many resorts offer complimentary sunrise yoga sessions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local fishing village by joining a guided walking tour or wandering independently. Watch fishermen mend nets, observe traditional boat-building, and browse a fresh seafood market. Learn about the local community's way of life.
day_by_day.evening: Join a street food tour led by a local guide. Walk through the town's food lanes and sample 8-10 different dishes across multiple stalls. Street food tours typically cost 500-800 THB and are an excellent way to discover hidden gems.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast — tropical fruit bowl, yogurt, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at the fishing village market — choose your fish and have it cooked on the spot (150-250 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food tour dinner — sample pad see ew, crispy pork belly with rice, kanom buang (crispy crepes), and fresh sugarcane juice across multiple stalls

day_by_day.notes: Street food tours are best booked through reputable local operators. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Inform the guide of any dietary restrictions or allergies in advance. Carry hand sanitizer for hygiene.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby national park or marine national park. Explore jungle trails, spot wildlife including monkeys, hornbills, and exotic butterflies. Visit a scenic waterfall and swim in a natural freshwater pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Join a ranger-led tour to learn about local flora and fauna. Visit a limestone cave system with impressive stalactites and stalagmites. Many national parks have entry fees of 200-500 THB for foreigners.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a relaxing evening. Treat yourself to a herbal compress massage or aromatherapy treatment at the hotel spa. Dine at the resort restaurant for convenience.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast to fuel the day's hiking
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local deli or restaurant near the park entrance — sandwiches, fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — try a Thai-Western fusion dish or a classic Thai set menu for 350-500 THB

day_by_day.notes: Wear lightweight long pants and a long-sleeved shirt for jungle hiking to protect against insects and sun. Bring insect repellent, sunscreen, and plenty of water. Start early to avoid afternoon heat and potential rain showers.

day_by_day.morning: Second major island hopping excursion to a different island group than Day 4. Explore new snorkeling spots, sea caves, and beaches. Consider a kayaking tour through dramatic limestone karst formations rising from the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a secluded beach accessible only by boat. Spend time swimming, reading, and relaxing in a paradise setting. Explore a coral garden with your snorkel gear and marvel at the underwater world.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise back to the mainland. Enjoy drinks on deck as the sky turns brilliant shades of orange and pink. Many sunset cruises include snacks and a complimentary drink for 600-1000 THB.

meals.breakfast: Quick resort breakfast or grab-and-go from a nearby bakery
meals.lunch: Tour-provided lunch on the boat or at a beach restaurant on the island — seafood fried rice and fresh fruit (150-200 THB)
meals.dinner: Waterfront restaurant with sea views — order a whole steamed fish with ginger and soy sauce, stir-fried morning glory, and jasmine rice (300-450 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book sunset cruises in advance, especially during peak season. Bring a light jacket for the boat ride back as evenings can be breezy on the water. Bring a camera with waterproof casing or a dry bag for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local market for souvenir shopping. Browse handcrafted goods including Thai silk, ceramic pottery, wood carvings, and silver jewelry. Practice your bargaining skills — start at 50-60% of the asking price and negotiate respectfully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a Thai fruit carving or traditional craft workshop. Learn the intricate art of carving elaborate designs into tropical fruits and vegetables, a centuries-old Thai tradition. Workshops cost 300-600 THB and you get to take your creation home.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farewell-style beach dinner as the trip winds down. Find a romantic beachfront restaurant, order your favorite Thai dishes from the trip, and reflect on your experiences. Toast to a wonderful journey.

meals.breakfast: Street-side breakfast at the market — try pa tong go (Thai-style fried dough) dipped in pandan custard with hot soy milk (50-80 THB)
meals.lunch: Food court at the market — assemble a meal from multiple stalls including curry, noodles, and fresh juice for under 150 THB
meals.dinner: Upscale beachfront restaurant — splurge on a seafood feast including tiger prawns, crab, and fresh fish with Thai herbs and sauces (600-900 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: When bargaining at markets, always be respectful and smile. Never lowball aggressively. If a vendor accepts your price, you are obligated to buy. Keep receipts for any high-value purchases for customs declaration.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — wake up early for a sunrise walk along the beach. Take photos, collect shells, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere before the day gets busy. Take a final swim in the warm tropical waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit any remaining attractions or places you missed during the trip. Revisit a favorite beach, temple, or market. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs or gifts. Pack your bags and organize your belongings for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Thailand — choose a restaurant that represents your favorite meal of the trip and recreate that magic one last time. Share photos and memories with travel companions.

meals.breakfast: Special resort breakfast — treat yourself to the full spread including fresh tropical juices, pastries, and a cooked Thai breakfast
meals.lunch: Casual local restaurant — order a comforting bowl of khao soi (northern Thai curry noodle soup) or your favorite noodle dish (100-150 THB)
meals.dinner: Your favorite restaurant from the trip revisited, or a new spot recommended by locals — budget 400-600 THB for a memorable final meal

day_by_day.notes: Check out procedures and arrange transportation to the airport for your departure. Confirm your flight details and allow extra time for check-in. Keep some Thai Baht for last-minute expenses but exchange remaining currency before leaving.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand. Enjoy a last breakfast at the resort or a nearby café. Take a final stroll along the beach or through the town. Visit a local temple for a quiet moment of reflection and gratitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for the airport with plenty of time to spare. Check in for your flight, clear security, and browse duty-free shops for any last-minute purchases. Thai duty-free offers excellent deals on Thai silk, herbal products, and spirits.
day_by_day.evening: Board your flight home, carrying wonderful memories of Thailand's stunning beaches, vibrant street food culture, and warm hospitality. Begin planning your return trip!

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — a bowl of jok (rice porridge) with ginger and a soft-boiled egg, or fresh fruit and coffee at a beachside café
meals.lunch: Airport food court or a quick meal before departure — try one last serving of pad thai or green curry
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant if time permits before boarding

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before an international flight. Declare any food items, plants, or high-value goods at customs. Thailand prohibits the export of certain Buddha images and antiques without a permit. Keep all receipts and documentation organized for customs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in with welcome champagne and traditional Thai floral garland greeting. Late-night turndown service and resort orientation with personal butler.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome snack platter and herbal teas arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Request early check-in amenities or a late-night snack arrangement with the resort concierge in advance. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a private guided orientation walk along the beachfront property. Settle into your villa, unpack, and enjoy the infinity pool overlooking the ocean. Book spa and excursion appointments for the week with your personal butler.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on the resort's private beach with complimentary sun loungers and butler service. Explore the immediate beachside area and nearby coastal promenade on foot. Enjoy a refreshing coconut drink and light snacks served beachside.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's overwater bar. Stroll to a nearby upscale beachfront restaurant for a relaxed first dinner. Return to resort for a welcome amenity — perhaps a traditional Thai herbal bath drawn by the butler.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant featuring tropical fruits, Thai congee, eggs Benedict, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Beachside light lunch at the resort's beach club — grilled tiger prawns, green papaya salad, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Upscale beachfront restaurant near the resort featuring fresh seafood platters, tom yum soup, and Thai-style grilled fish with panoramic ocean views

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Use this time to plan the rest of the trip with your concierge. October in Thailand may bring occasional rain showers — pack a light waterproof jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat charter from the resort's pier for a morning island-hopping excursion to nearby uninhabited islands. Snorkel in crystal-clear waters, explore hidden coves, and photograph dramatic limestone karsts. Bring a packed gourmet picnic basket prepared by the resort chef.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping to a second island with a pristine white sand beach. Enjoy swimming, kayaking, and paddleboarding in calm turquoise waters. Visit a sea cave or lagoon accessible only by boat for a truly exclusive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and head to a premium street food night market for an authentic local culinary adventure. Try pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay skewers, and fresh-squeezed sugarcane juice.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort — Thai-style omelette with jasmine rice, fresh tropical fruit bowl, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on a private island — charcuterie board, fresh sandwiches, tropical fruits, and chilled sparkling water prepared by the resort chef
meals.dinner: Premium local night market street food experience — sample 6–8 dishes including grilled seafood, som tum, roti with condensed milk, and mango sticky rice

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the private boat charter 24 hours in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkeling gear (or rent from the resort), and a waterproof camera. The night market is best experienced on foot — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga or Muay Thai introductory class on the resort's beachfront pavilion led by a certified instructor. Follow with a Thai herbal steam bath and 60-minute traditional Thai massage at the resort spa. Enjoy a healthy smoothie bowl post-treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private longtail boat trip to a nearby coral reef for world-class snorkeling or beginner scuba diving with a certified PADI instructor. Explore vibrant marine life including parrotfish, sea turtles, and colorful coral gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Private candlelit dinner on the beach arranged by the resort — a bespoke Thai tasting menu curated by the executive chef, served under the stars with personalized service.

meals.breakfast: Healthy resort breakfast — acai bowl, avocado toast, chia pudding, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort beach club post-diving — grilled barramundi, steamed jasmine rice, and a fresh mango salad
meals.dinner: Exclusive private beach dinner — 7-course Thai tasting menu featuring massaman lamb, blue swimmer crab curry, pandan-infused desserts, and premium Thai wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa treatment and private beach dinner at least 48 hours in advance. For scuba diving, bring or request a medical disclaimer form. This is a perfect romantic evening option.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat day trip to a famous nearby island (such as Koh Phi Phi, Koh Lanta, or Koh Lipe depending on resort location). Arrive early before day-trippers to enjoy the beaches in near-solitude. Hike to a viewpoint for panoramic island photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island's village on foot — browse artisan shops, taste local snacks, and interact with friendly locals. Swim at the island's most iconic beach. Enjoy a leisurely lunch at a cliffside restaurant with sweeping sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by speedboat at sunset for a golden-hour arrival. Enjoy cocktails at the resort bar while watching the sunset. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the resort before departure — croissants, tropical fruits, yogurt parfait, and espresso
meals.lunch: Cliffside restaurant on the island — fresh whole grilled snapper, coconut rice, stir-fried morning glory, and fresh lime soda
meals.dinner: Resort signature fine-dining restaurant — Thai-French fusion cuisine, premium seafood, and curated wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (7:00–7:30 AM) to maximize time on the island and avoid crowds. Pre-arrange the private speedboat charter through the resort concierge. Bring cash for local market purchases on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayaking tour through mangrove forests and sea caves with a private guide. Observe local wildlife including kingfishers, monitor lizards, and tropical birds. A truly immersive and serene natural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely poolside afternoon. Indulge in a couple's or solo 90-minute aromatherapy massage at the spa. Enjoy a private pool villa experience if available — sip champagne and read in absolute tranquility.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local town's street food scene with a private Thai street food tour guide. Visit 4–5 street food stalls curated for quality and authenticity — try boat noodles, crispy pork belly rice, Thai iced tea, and grilled corn with coconut cream.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before kayaking — banana, granola bar, and coffee from the resort
meals.lunch: Post-spa poolside lunch — club sandwich, watermelon feta salad, fresh coconut, and iced hibiscus tea
meals.dinner: Guided street food tour — 5–6 curated dishes across multiple stalls, including pad kra pao, boat noodles, grilled pork skewers, and Thai rolled ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The kayaking tour is best at sunrise (5:30–6:00 AM departure) for calm waters and wildlife sightings. Book the street food tour guide through the concierge for a vetted local expert experience.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private yacht charter begins. Board a luxury catamaran or sailing yacht from the resort marina. Set sail toward a cluster of remote islands with a captain, crew, and private chef on board. Morning sailing with fresh fruit platters and mimosas on deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anchor at a secluded bay for swimming, snorkeling, and paddleboarding. The onboard chef prepares a fresh Thai seafood BBQ lunch on the yacht deck. Sail to a second destination — perhaps a hidden beach or floating village — for afternoon exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Sail back toward the resort as the sun sets over the Andaman Sea or Gulf of Thailand. Enjoy sundowner cocktails on deck with a stunning golden-hour backdrop. Disembark and enjoy a quiet dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Onboard continental spread — fresh fruits, pastries, smoked salmon, and mimosas
meals.lunch: Freshly prepared Thai seafood BBQ on the yacht deck — grilled lobster, tiger prawns, squid, sticky rice, and green mango salad
meals.dinner: Casual resort dinner at the beachside terrace restaurant — tom kha gai, pad see ew, and coconut ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The private yacht charter is the highlight of the trip — book well in advance (at least 1 week prior). Bring seasickness medication if needed, a wide-brimmed hat, and a waterproof bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Enjoy a slow breakfast and light stretching or meditation session on the beach. Visit the resort's wellness center for a detox juice consultation or Thai herbal compress treatment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a private Thai cooking class at a nearby luxury cooking school or hosted by the resort chef. Learn to prepare 4–5 classic Thai dishes including tom yum soup, green curry, mango sticky rice, and spring rolls. Take home a recipe card booklet.
day_by_day.evening: Dine on the meal you prepared during the cooking class in a private garden setting. Enjoy a post-dinner stroll along the beachfront promenade. End the evening with a nightcap at the resort's rooftop or overwater bar.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — eggs your way, fresh-pressed juices, tropical fruits, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch before the cooking class — fresh spring rolls, papaya salad, and iced lemongrass tea
meals.dinner: Enjoy the 4-course meal prepared during your Thai cooking class, served in a private garden setting with Thai sparkling wine

day_by_day.notes: The Thai cooking class is a memorable and educational experience. Most premium classes include a market visit in the morning to source ingredients — confirm with the organizer. Great activity for solo travelers and couples alike.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat transfer to a nearby floating fishing village or stilted sea village. Walk through the village on elevated wooden walkways, visit the local mosque or temple, and observe traditional fishing practices. Purchase handcrafted souvenirs directly from local artisans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a nearby deserted sandbar that appears only at low tide — a magical, ephemeral experience. Enjoy a bottle of champagne and fresh seafood snacks on the sandbar with your private guide. Swim in the surrounding shallow turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Enjoy a premium beachfront seafood dinner at a renowned local restaurant. Try whole steamed crab, grilled scallops, and Thai-style lobster with garlic and pepper.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Thai-style fried rice with egg, fresh papaya, and green tea
meals.lunch: Sandbar picnic — champagne, fresh oysters, tiger prawns, cold cuts, artisan bread, and tropical fruits
meals.dinner: Premium beachfront seafood restaurant — whole steamed Dungeness crab, grilled scallops, tom yum seafood soup, and jasmine rice

day_by_day.notes: The sandbar visit is tide-dependent — confirm timing with your guide the evening before. Bring waterproof sandals for walking in shallow water and a waterproof bag for electronics.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to a local floating market or traditional Thai wet market with a private guide. Taste exotic tropical fruits, freshly made Thai sweets, and hot street snacks. Learn about local ingredients and culinary traditions from vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure — choose between a second spa treatment, resort pool relaxation, or a private guided snorkeling session at a nearby coral reef. Alternatively, explore a nearby national park or nature reserve on a guided walk.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktail experience — a private mixology class at the resort bar learning to make classic Thai cocktails (lychee mojito, tamarind whiskey sour, and pandan gin tonic). Followed by a premium dinner at the resort's fine-dining venue.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — freshly made Thai crepes (khanom buang), grilled corn, fresh coconut jelly, and hot Thai tea
meals.lunch: Resort pool lunch — grilled chicken satay, noodle salad, watermelon juice, and a cheese board
meals.dinner: Resort fine-dining — 5-course tasting menu with wine pairing featuring Thai-inspired contemporary cuisine

day_by_day.notes: The floating market is usually most vibrant early morning (6:00–9:00 AM). Arrange a tuk-tuk or private car transfer with the resort. Bring small denomination Thai baht for market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to a world-famous national park or marine sanctuary (such as Ang Thong Marine Park, Similan Islands, or Khao Sok National Park depending on location). Depart by private speedboat or seaplane for a truly premium arrival experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike through lush jungle trails to a hidden lagoon or freshwater lake with stunning panoramic views. Swim in emerald green waters surrounded by towering limestone cliffs. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort in a scenic jungle clearing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing evening — perhaps a sunset beach walk and a quiet dinner at the resort's casual beachside eatery. Reflect on the journey over a glass of fine Thai rum or local craft beer.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — banana pancakes, boiled eggs, fruit platter, and espresso
meals.lunch: Gourmet jungle picnic — artisan sandwiches, Thai rice salads, tropical fruits, sparkling water, and fresh-baked cookies
meals.dinner: Casual resort beachside dinner — grilled fish tacos with Thai slaw, sweet potato fries, and fresh coconut shake

day_by_day.notes: The Similan Islands are a UNESCO-protected marine sanctuary — follow all conservation guidelines. A seaplane transfer (if available) provides a spectacular aerial view of the archipelago and is worth the premium cost.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning spa indulgence — a 2-hour royal Thai ritual featuring a body scrub, herbal wrap, and full-body massage. Enjoy a post-treatment healthy breakfast in the spa garden. Spend the remaining morning hours floating in the resort's infinity pool with a cocktail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at a curated luxury boutique or artisan craft market near the resort. Purchase Thai silk scarves, handmade ceramics, artisan jewelry, or premium Thai spice sets. Pack thoughtfully for the return journey.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — the resort's most exclusive dining experience, perhaps a private chef's table or a rooftop dinner with 360-degree ocean views. Toast to the trip with a bottle of premium Champagne and a bespoke dessert.

meals.breakfast: Spa garden breakfast — fresh fruit, granola, Greek yogurt, herbal teas, and cold-pressed green juice
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — club sandwich, watermelon salad, and iced passion fruit tea
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner — private chef's table or rooftop fine-dining with a 7-course Thai-inspired tasting menu, Champagne toast, and custom dessert

day_by_day.notes: Request the farewell dinner arrangement at least 3 days in advance. Consider purchasing premium Thai products such as single-origin Thai coffee, artisan hot sauces, or silk textiles as gifts. Begin packing tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the beach to soak in the last moments of paradise. Enjoy a leisurely checkout breakfast at the resort. Complete checkout formalities with the personal butler — luggage handling and transport arrangements confirmed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to the airport. Arrive with ample time for premium check-in, lounge access, and duty-free shopping. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of beaches, island hopping, and culinary discovery.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Thailand. Carry beautiful memories, a full photo gallery, new culinary skills, and perhaps a jar of Thai green curry paste for home.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — go all out with the full buffet spread, fresh-made omelets, tropical fruits, and a farewell Thai iced coffee
meals.lunch: Airport business or first-class lounge dining — light Thai-inspired bites or international fare
meals.dinner: Inflight dining or airport restaurant pre-departure

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort (typically 12:00 PM). Request a late checkout if your flight departs in the evening. Keep all receipts for customs declarations if purchasing high-value items. Ensure all travel documents, passports, and boarding passes are organized the night before.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
